lesson.title: USGA Golf Club CT Compliance Test
lesson.buzzAssessmentTitle: Unit 3 Lesson 2: USGA Golf Club CT Compliance Test

gradingDesign.rule: Only lessons with a completed provided chart use 10 automatic points; variable student evidence is graded in the final two BusyBee responses.

questions.prompt: The graph shows the force the ball exerts on the club. Which graph represents the force the club exerts on the ball during the same collision?
Why does the golf ball accelerate much more than the club without violating Newton's Third Law?
Record the Soft Polymer contact time from the force-time trace. ________ microseconds
Record the Alloy contact time from the force-time trace. ________ microseconds
Record the Thin Titanium contact time from the force-time trace. ________ microseconds
Record the Thick Titanium contact time from the force-time trace. ________ microseconds
Record the Soft Polymer peak force from the force-time trace. ________ kN
Record the Thick Titanium peak force from the force-time trace. ________ kN
Record the Rigid Steel contact time. ________ microseconds
Record the Prototype X-7 contact time. ________ microseconds

Use at least three entries from your completed chart to explain how contact time and force change from the softer faces to the stiffer faces. Then state what stays approximately constant about the impulse.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Look for a data-supported trend and the force-time area connection.
a. Full credit: Cites at least three correct chart values, explains that stiffer faces have shorter contact times and larger forces, and states that the force-time areas or impulses are approximately equal.
  Partial credit: Gives the correct trend with limited numerical evidence or omits the impulse connection.
  No credit: Gives no chart evidence or reverses the main trend.

questions.prompt: Make the final USGA compliance ruling for Rigid Steel and Prototype X-7 using the CT limit of 257 microseconds. Support the ruling with both measured contact times and connect the interaction to Newton's Third Law.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: The ruling must use the standard, both measurements, and the interaction-force relationship.
a. Full credit: States that Rigid Steel at about 147 microseconds is compliant and Prototype X-7 at about 266 microseconds is not, compares both values with the 257-microsecond limit, and explains that club and ball exert equal-magnitude opposite forces.
  Partial credit: Makes the correct ruling but omits one measurement or the Newton's Third Law connection.
  No credit: Reverses the compliance ruling or provides no measurement evidence.
